messages:
Anna: Heads-up — we've started seeing a spike of 'orphan' traces from async workers (lots of new root spans). Looks correlated with retry/redrive flows on SQS. Anyone seen this pattern?
Sasha: Yup saw that in perf dash. 50% of retries create a fresh trace id instead of continuing parent.
Mike: Repro'd locally — our retryer republishes messages but I only passed MessageBody to sendMessage. Oops. MessageAttributes (where we stash traceparent) are not copied by default.
Anna: That's probably it. On initial publish we put `traceparent` in MessageAttributes so the gateway and worker connect spans. If we republish without attributes we lose context.
Sasha: Confirmed: sample from prod DLQ shows bodies with `retry_count` but missing `traceparent`. Example: ```MessageAttributes: { "traceparent": { "DataType": "String", "StringValue": "00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01" } }```
Lee: Nice find. Two places: 1) our worker retry logic that calls SQS sendMessage, 2) the dead-letter-forwarding lambda that republishes. Both copies currently omit attributes.
Zarina: For a quick fix we can: a) change send wrappers to always copy MessageAttributes when republishing, b) as a fallback embed a small `__trace` JSON in the body so republishers that only pass body still preserve context. Prefer (a) long-term.
Mike: Agree. (a) is cleaner. Also we should canonicalize key name to `traceparent` not `x-traceparent` so OTEL libs handle it.
Anna: Note: some of our services were using `tracestate` + `traceparent`. We should copy all attributes that start with `trace` (case-insensitive) to be safe.
Sasha: Another edge: our OTLP exporter batching groups spans and sometimes exports before the worker finishes, so if root is missing we lose links. Adding attribute copy reduces new roots, but we should also add `links` on span creation when we detect a trace id in body.
Lee: Will do. Plan: PR to redwood-async lib to "preserve_message_attributes_on_republish" + unit tests, and a separate tiny PR to the DLQ forwarder. I'll own both.
Anna: Add a small telemetry query to detect regressions: count spans where `parent_id` is null AND `resource.service.name = async-worker` in last 1h. Alert if > 5 per 5m.
Zarina: Also add a small lint in infra pipeline to warn if sendMessage is called without `MessageAttributes`. Could be a static check in our SDK wrapper.
Mike: I'll mock a repro and attach logs to the PR. Repro steps: 1) publish message with traceattr, 2) worker fails and republish without attrs, 3) check tracing UI for orphan span.
Anna: Deploy-bot: pushed canary of redwood-async/republish-fix to staging at 2026-03-18T11:42Z (build #4342).
deploy-bot: Deployment succeeded: redwood-async 0.23.1 -> staging :sparkles: (link: https://deploys/revision/4342)
Sasha: Deployed to staging — initial test looks good, traceparent preserved on retry.
Lee: PRs: redwood-async#612 (copy attrs), dlq-forwarder#98 (copy attrs fallback). I'll add tests & QA notes.
Anna: Thanks — assign to QA for validation and schedule a prod rollout Weds EOD if staging stays stable. :thumbsup:
